subject.title: [Feature]: Audio file support in read tool (multimodal parity with images)

question: Should OpenClaw add native audio attachments to the core read-tool/model-input contract, and what raw-media egress, provider serialization, fallback, payload-limit, and transcript/audit policy should govern it?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-proven, but the permanent contract changes provider routing, raw local-media forwarding, Codex compatibility, and session state semantics that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Design native-audio contract first
options.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider transports, explicit raw-media egress, byte limits, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

options.title: Keep read audio unsupported for now
options.body: Leave raw audio out of the read tool and direct users to existing transcription/media-understanding paths until maintainers are ready to own native audio egress.

options.title: Fold into native-audio tracker
options.body: Treat this read-tool request as a subcase of #51667 if maintainers want one broader native-audio product design thread.

recommendation.title: Design native-audio contract first
recommendation.body: Settle typed audio blocks, provider transports, explicit raw-media egress, byte limits, unsupported-model behavior, and transcript/audit metadata before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history signal across media understanding and the product/security boundary this decision would change.
